text: Semi-commercial farmers who keep poultry confined must supply all feed, using complete commercial feed, a concentrate mixed with local raw materials (about 20% concentrate), or home-mixed raw materials plus additives (vitamins, minerals, amino acids). Across all systems, feeding young chickens commercial feed until 21 days is recommended to ensure a strong, deficiency-free start. Common raw materials for complementary feeding of scavenging poultry: rice and rice by-products (broken rice, boiled rice, paddy, rice bran — the most common supplement, providing energy; rice bran also gives 8–12% protein and is rich in phosphorus and vitamin B); corn (should ideally be the base of supplementary feeding, though uncommon in Cambodia — crushed corn gives good energy plus 9–10% protein, and its pigments boost the yellow color of skin and egg yolks); and banana stems (commonly used but of limited nutritional value, being low in protein).
